## GATE1 · GATE1-composed-r10 — GATE1 with K10: R10 and the deadline notice still miss in the composed lease

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 9

Decision references: 096645668

Evidence: Bisect (.wash/local/GATE1-r10-bisect.md): the handle sweep costs 35.5 µs per live handle system-wide (the 2x); a lone lease costs ~56 ms from kill, the owner walk and the notice walk. Design committed 096645668 (docs/kernel/budgets.md residual items 3 and 5): reverse chains per budget for handles held outside, dying tables freed whole, a process's frames found from its page tables, and cheaper endpoint release and notice walk. Acceptance is the gate's full fill (MAX_HANDLES) at 30/40/125 ms with H no slower than D; if the floor misses, K12 stops with the phase table and preemptible reclamation goes to the owner. Fill = full handle table; ring = 2048 pages (done in 4c64716dd).

> 
> (2) The fill: grow the lease. Settled by the Containment page ("room added for a full handle table") and the owner's no-weakening guard. Size CT_LEASE_PAGES so the table reaches MAX_HANDLES with the rest endpoints, computed once in the program. The fill ends when the kernel refuses a handle because the table is full, not because pages ran out. No page change.
> Consequence: about 4,000 endpoints at ~15 µs each is about 60 ms of teardown alone, so removing scans cannot reach 30 ms. K12 is size L: it must cut the per-object cost several times, or bound the non-preemptible part, keeping I1, I2 and I10 exact. If neither reaches 30 ms, I take it to the owner with the numbers.
> 
> (3) The ring: one bigger constant. trace::PAGES goes from 512 to 2048 (8 MiB, 262K records, against ~172K needed), as K12's step 0 with scheduling.md's '2 MiB' line. GATE1 may carry it on scratch to measure. Rejected: per-case sizing (a second knob) and a bounded window (a miss could hide outside it). 'dropped 0' stays.
> 
> (c) Agreed.

> - kill 31.8 | 30.0 ms: process_ended/close_all_handles 11928, release_all_memory 10783, process_ending ~7.8k
> - owner walk 12964
> - abandoned-notice walk 6014 | 5834

> Curve, H's sweep vs neighbour's live handles: 1 → 5669; 512 → 23806; 1024 → 41944 (1024 mints: 42012); 1531 → 59616. That is 35.5 µs per live handle anywhere in the system: the sweep walks every process's table. It is the 2x, the last whole-system scan.
> 
> Own size (dying lease): kill +7.6 µs per own handle (1 → 18.3 ms, 1531 → 30.0); owner walk 9.1 µs per own endpoint (153 → 12964); deferred frees 0.9 µs per endpoint. Own threads +16: +2.2 ms. Own pages +1000: +0.19 ms. Neighbour pages: 0. Neighbour threads +16: +2.2 ms in the pid x tid walks.

> So even a subtree-keyed sweep leaves a lone full lease at ~56 ms vs 30. Under 30 needs the sweep bounded plus lower per-handle close (skip per-slot remove for a table freed whole) and per-endpoint release, and the notice walk moved onto the dying endpoints' calls.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `22679554b463a22a38db379d8ce2a8d3` · 2026-09-30T23:59:36Z

> K12's design is committed on redoubt as 096645668: docs/kernel/budgets.md Residual risks, items 3 and 5 and the paragraph after them, marked not built. The brief is rewritten at .wash/local/K12-implementer.md with base 096645668. No owner choice was needed: this is the reverse index the K9 design named as the sweep's fallback ("arch, not owner; reopen here rather than widen").
> 
> - Item 3, the chains: a handle whose holder runs inside the budget it depends on dies with its holder's table. A handle held outside is entered, when it enters a table, in two doubly linked chains headed by that budget (its object's owner, its stamp). Destruction walks the dying budgets' chains, closes exactly those handles, and frees the dying tables whole. No live table is swept, so the H/D 2x goes. Slots grow to 8 words, 64 per page, which means one model constant (after MOD1).
> - Item 5: ending a process finds its frames from its page tables and kernel frames, not from the RAM-wide ownership array. That scan is ~5.4 ms per process, and R12 forbids terms linear in RAM.
> - Cost cuts: tables freed whole, cheaper endpoint release, and the notice walk joined to an existing thread walk.
> 
> Order: ring (done), frames, chains, costs, model constant, measuring after each with the bisect's T records. The acceptance is the gate's full-fill run at 30/40/125 ms, with H no slower than D. If the measured floor shows 30 ms is out of reach at the full fill, K12 stops with the phase table, and preemptible reclamation goes to the owner.
> 
> Required: an attack case with a handle held outside, several levels up and across, stamped by or naming the dying subtree. The checked build's audit must catch a planted missing chain entry (a test-only feature).
> 
> Resolve when ready. For GATE1, not K12: wait_arm's 30 s against a ~20 s arm, and a child's panic showing up as a fault (spawn copies the launcher's Console).
